# Lane S

A lane S change is worked from its own lane S ticket, in that ticket's worktree, never in the main checkout. It has
no intent interview, approval, approach, plan, executor or verify: you make the change yourself.

## Start

- New request: the accord skill ran `accord new ticket <id> --lane S --worktree`. Before you follow the `enter:` or
  `stop:` line it printed as `./worktree.md` says, write the title, the two lines of step 1 and the `## Scope` lines `./lane.md` describes into
  `<path>/accord/tickets/<id>.md`, asking step 1's question first when it needs one. Then run
  `git -C "<path>" commit -m "ticket: <id> understood" -- accord/tickets/<id>.md` and
  `git -C "<path>" push -u origin <branch>`. After `enter:`, go on at step 1 in that worktree; after `stop:`, the
  session opened there finds the two lines in the ticket.
- Pick up: run `accord worktree open <id>` and follow `./worktree.md`.
- Continue: `accord anchor` prints `Lane: S` and the stage. Resume at step 1 for `intent`, step 2 for `build`, step 4
  for `review`, and step 6 for `done`.

## Steps

1. **Understood.** When `## Understood` and `## Done when` in `accord/tickets/<id>.md` each hold a line, keep them.
   Otherwise write one line under `## Understood`: the change as you understood it, and one line under
   `## Done when`: the observable result that ends the work. Go on without waiting only when the request has a concrete anchor (file, symbol,
   error message, or expected behaviour) and one plausible reading; otherwise ask exactly one question, as
   `./ask.md` says, and wait. When `title:` still reads `Short title in business language`, replace it with a few
   words naming the change in business language. When `## Scope` holds no path, run step 1 of `./lane.md` and write its files there as its `## Scope` says. Run `accord gate ready <id>` and fix what it prints until it exits
   0, then commit the ticket. When it says a `depends_on` ticket is not done on the default branch, never remove that entry
   from `depends_on`: tell the owner this ticket waits for that ticket's merge, then after the merge run `git fetch` and
   `accord gate ready <id>` again. Make no other change before that. Never run `accord approve`.
2. **Change.** Make the change in this worktree. For a bug, first write a test that reproduces it and see it fail,
   then fix it. A test you add carries `risk:<kind>` in its name. A file outside `## Scope` that the change only
   rewords, in at most 3 lines, neither new nor deleted, needs the line `Wording-only: <path> — <reason>` under
   `## Rulings` in `accord/tickets/<id>/ledger.md` before the review. A `.md` record under `accord/research/` that the ticket lists under `research:` and this branch
   adds is the ticket's own file and needs no `## Scope` line. Any other file beyond `## Scope`, a listed
   sensitive area, or a sign of a new interface lifts the ticket to lane M.
3. **Tests.** Run the `tests.affected` command from `accord/config.yml` over the changed files, or `tests.full` when
   `tests.affected` is not configured or finds no test file. Fix what fails, then commit the change.
4. **Review rounds.** Round <n> runs `accord review-package <id>` into a file outside the working tree and
   dispatches one fresh `accord-reviewer`, lens `both`, with the paths of the ticket file, that file, and
   `accord/tickets/<id>/ledger.md` when it exists. Append what it reports to `accord/tickets/<id>/review.md` under
   `## Round <n> head <sha>`, `<sha>` being the `Head: <sha>` line the package printed and the heading ending
   ` (added code round 1)` when `accord round` printed `Added code:`; write each finding as
   `Must|Should|Nice <n>: <finding> — <path>[:<line>] | none — fixed in <sha> | deferred | open`, then its marks, or
   `No findings`; copy each
   `Confirmed wording-only: <path>` line it reports verbatim into that round, and commit
   `review.md` alone at once; when you stop after this round with no Must open, first append step 5's verdict, so
   the round and its verdict are one commit. When the round reports a Must, fix every Must and Should yourself, run
   step 3 again, commit, and start the next round with a new reviewer; a finding for a file outside `## Scope`
   with no `Wording-only` line, or for a sign of a new interface, is not fixed here: it starts the lift below.
   When it reports no Must open, either stop
   there, leaving its Shoulds open in the record, or fix them the same way and run another round: a fix no reviewer
   has seen never ships. There is no final reviewer and no model tier-up. At most five rounds, counted from the
   `## Round <n>` sections of `review.md`: when the fifth still reports a Must, commit its record, stop and report
   the open findings to the owner; never report the work finished. Resumed at `review`, the next round is one after
   the last `## Round <n>` in `review.md`; when that round reported a Must whose fix is not yet committed, make and
   commit the fix first.
   `review.md` starts with the line `Round record: 2`, above every heading. A `review.md` whose first round was committed while `accord/config.yml` pinned accord 0.3.0 or earlier keeps its `Round record: 1`, its `## Round <n>` headings and its finding lines, without heads or marks, and keeps that form after a merge of the default branch. A finding line starts with its severity word, `Must`, `Should` or `Nice`, never two of them or a question mark. After its state a finding line carries its marks, each after ` — `: `carried from <r>.<n>` when round `<r>` of this cycle reported it as finding `<n>`; `risk: data-loss` or `risk: security`; `test: <test id>` or `command: <command>` when a failing test or a command reproduces it; `rests on: Understood "<quote>"` or `rests on: Done when "<quote>"`, a quote of at least three words. From round 3, for a file a merge's own changes touched counted from the round headed `(added code round 1)`, a Must or Should not carried from an earlier round, whose location is not a file your previous fix changed, blocks only with `test:`, `command:` or a `risk:` mark; otherwise write it `deferred` with the line `- review <r>.<n> cycle <k>: <finding>` under `## Deferred` in `accord/tickets/<id>/ledger.md` (` cycle <k>` from cycle 2 on), and it leaves the stop. From round 3 a new Should also needs `rests on:`, `test:`, `command:` or a `risk:` mark, or is written as a Nice. Each file a commit after a round changes, up to the next round, but a merge of the default branch and a commit that changes only the ticket's records, is the location of a finding of that round, or a Ruling in the ledger names its path with a reason. Before each round, and before appending step 5's verdict, run `accord round <id>`: exit 0 prints the round's number and the cap, counting the `## Round <n>` sections after the last `## Return from verify` line. It prints `stop: report to owner` from round 3 on a round that still reports a Should or a Must, and at the cap: commit the round's record, stop and report the open findings to the owner with what it prints, and write the owner's answer as the last line `verdict: accepted-by-owner "<the owner's words>"`, as the ledger Ruling `Ruling: the owner allows <n> more review rounds after round <r> of cycle <k> — "<the owner's words>" — <cost if wrong>`, or as the lift to lane M below, which is the change of course in lane S. Before the verdict, a stop whose only `Reason:` is that the cap is reached and no owner Ruling allows more lets the verdict be written. On `refused:`, fix what it names and run it again. Resumed at `review` with `review.md` ending in a verdict and a commit made after it, first run `git log -1 --format=%H -- accord/tickets/<id>/review.md` and append `## Return from verify <sha>` with the sha it prints; the rounds after it count from 1.
5. **Verdict.** The last line of `review.md` is `verdict: converged` when the last round reported no Must open, or
   `verdict: accepted-by-owner "<the owner's words>"` when the owner accepts the open findings at the cap or at a stop from round 3; that one
   is committed alone, right after that round's record. Nothing follows that line. `accord gate done` fails on
   any commit after the last round's record that changes more than the ticket's records: a change after it needs
   another round and a new verdict.
6. **Pull request.** When `tests.report` is set in `accord/config.yml` and `tests.affected` does not write it, run
   `tests.full` first so the gate finds a fresh report. Run `accord gate done <id>` and fix what it prints. Push the branch with
   `git push -u origin <branch>` and open a pull request with `gh pr create --fill` when `gh` is available, otherwise
   ask the owner to open it. It waits for the owner's merge. Report the finish as `./finish.md` says.

## Lift to lane M

When the work meets a lift condition in `./lane.md`, a reviewer finds a file outside `## Scope` with no `Wording-only` line or a sign of a new interface, or `accord gate done <id>` names a file outside `## Scope`, a sensitive area or a sign of a new interface, or says `## Scope` held no path, stop and say which one. On the owner's yes, in this same
ticket, branch and worktree:

1. In `accord/tickets/<id>.md`, change `lane: S` to `lane: M` and add the lane M sections, each empty, after the
   existing ones: `## Intent`, `## Acceptance criteria`, `## Vetoes`, `## Decisions`, `## Corrections` when absent,
   then the open questions and approach sections the lane M template has.
2. Remove `accord/tickets/<id>/review.md` with `git rm` when it exists.
3. Run `git merge-base HEAD <origin's default branch>` and write into `accord/tickets/<id>/ledger.md`, under
   `## Rulings`: `Ruling: lifted from lane S; the plan baseline is the fork point <sha> — the review then reads the lane S code too — cost if wrong: that code goes unreviewed`.
4. Commit, then load `accord-intent` and start the intent interview. Code already committed stays on the branch.

## Rules

- A correction from the owner goes verbatim under `## Corrections` in the ticket, added with the first one, before
  any other action.
- Every decision that is not the owner's is a Ruling in `accord/tickets/<id>/ledger.md` under `## Rulings`:
  `Ruling: <what> — <why> — <cost if wrong>`.
